archetypes.name: meta-contract
archetypes.rationale: Targets positional .meta contract drift across launcher writers and retry consumers, the highest-risk proposed-change surface in this plan.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit whether the plan preserves the external_launcher_append_outer_meta positional contract across every writer and consumer it touches. Compare the proposed risk and stderr_sink argument threading against the helper implementation, launch-review lanes, cursor launchers, and collector retry paths. Look for missing callers, swapped optional arguments, default behavior changes, or plan claims that do not match repo evidence. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-realism
archetypes.rationale: Focuses on whether the proposed static-grep replacement actually proves runtime forwarding instead of recording a stub artifact.
archetypes.prompt_body: Evaluate the proposed behavioral test changes for whether they truly observe runtime argv delivery on the intended paths. Check the existing test harnesses, stubs, temp files, and retry fixtures to see whether the plan can assert --stderr-sink and --risk without false positives from setup-only strings or unrelated invocations. Pay special attention to codex versus cursor lane symmetry and outer-launcher versus CMD_JSON retry coverage. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: doc-sync
archetypes.rationale: Checks whether the plan’s documentation scope matches repository sibling-doc and flag-contract expectations.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review whether the plan updates the correct documentation for the changed launcher behavior and omits only genuinely behavior-neutral docs. Compare launch-review.md, nearby script documentation conventions, and any sibling-doc rules that apply to the touched scripts. Look for cross-doc inconsistency around --risk, OUTER_LAUNCHER_RISK, stderr sink forwarding, and retry semantics. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
